question.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3},{X}_{4}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼B(7,\theta )$ with unknown probability of success $\theta .$ You're given the particular sample 

$$
{x}_{1}=6,\,{x}_{2}=1,\,{x}_{3}=2,\,{x}_{4}=7.
$$

The log-likelihood function of the sample is given by

$$
l(\theta )=\operatorname{ln}⁡a+b\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +c\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ).
$$

Find the value of $a+b+c.$

*Hint: The probability mass function for a binomial random variable is given by*

$$
f(x)=(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{x}){\theta }^{x}(1-\theta )^{7-x},\,x=0,1,…,7.
$$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed discrete random variables with probability mass function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the log-likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡L(\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i},\theta )) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(f({x}_{i},\theta )).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=4$ independent binomial random variables with an unknown probability of success $\theta $ and $N=7$ as the number of trials. Therefore, the probability mass function is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,\theta ) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{N}{x}){\theta }^{x}(1-\theta )^{N-x},\,x=0,1,…,N \\  & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{x}){\theta }^{x}(1-\theta )^{7-x},\,x=0,1,…,7.\end{aligned}
$$

We can calculate the log-likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡((\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{i}}){\theta }^{{x}_{i}}(1-\theta )^{7-{x}_{i}}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{i}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡({\theta }^{{x}_{i}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡((1-\theta )^{7-{x}_{i}}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{i}})+{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(7-{x}_{i})\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{i}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}+\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ){\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(7-{x}_{i}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{i}})+S\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(7n-S)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta )\end{aligned}
$$

where $S={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}.$

Now, note that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{i}}) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{1}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{2}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{3}})+\operatorname{ln}⁡(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{4}}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{i}})).\end{aligned}
$$

So, our expression for $l(\theta )$ becomes

$$
l(\theta )=\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{i}}))+S\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(7n-S)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ).
$$

Now, using the sample data with $n=4,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\prod }_{i=1}^{n}(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{{x}_{i}}) & =(\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{6})\cdot (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{1})\cdot (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{2})\cdot (\genfrac{}{}{0pt}{}{7}{7}) \\  & =7\cdot 7\cdot 21\cdot 1 \\  & =1\,029,\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
S=6+1+2+7=16.
$$

Substituting the above values into our expression for $l(\theta )$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(1\,029)+16\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(7\cdot 4-16)\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡1\,029+16\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +12\operatorname{ln}⁡(1-\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
a+b+c=1\,029+16+12=1\,057.
$$
